card.name: Cueca
card.era: Late 18th century to present; form consolidated by late 19th century
card.profile: A couples courtship dance in which partners wave handkerchiefs and trace circular figures, turns and half-turns, evoking the courtship of a rooster and hen (Britannica; Wikipedia). Danced to guitar, accordion, guitarron, harp, tambourine and handclaps, in alternating 6/8-3/4 with hemiola; structured in cuarteta, seguidilla and remate. Central to the September Fiestas Patrias; widely held to descend from the Peruvian zamacueca. Declared Chile's national dance by Decree No. 23 (Diario Oficial, 6 November 1979) (Marca Chile; Wikipedia).
card.insight: The Pinochet dictatorship's official promotion of cueca from 1979 reshaped its imagery; in protest the cueca sola debuted on 8 March 1978 in Santiago by the folk ensemble of the Association of Families of the Detained-Disappeared (AFDD), per Chile's Museo de la Memoria y los Derechos Humanos.
